title: Dedicated SLA negotiation playbook for bursty RLHF & fine-tune workloads
text:
Dedicated SLA negotiation playbook for bursty RLHF & fine-tune workloads

description:
Create a negotiation & intake playbook tailored to enterprise customers whose primary workloads are bursty Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) training/evaluation and iterative fine-tuning. The playbook should: (1) capture workload fingerprints for peak/steady token throughput and checkpoint-warming behavior; (2) prescribe GPU class and reservation sizing heuristics; (3) define SLA terms (latency P50/P95, committed throughput, burst credits) and acceptable fallback model tiers; and (4) include an onboarding checklist and negotiation scripts for Sales and Solutions Engineers.

background:
We have recurring enterprise requests where customers need dedicated pools for GenAI training/eval loops or fine-tuning pipelines that show long periods of low activity punctuated by high-intensity bursts (e.g., nightly RLHF rollouts, multi-step human evaluation batches). Existing intake artifacts are oriented toward steady inference throughput; they under-spec the unique warm-up, checkpoint IO, KV cache priming, and cross-GPU communication patterns of RLHF/fine-tuning. This doc bridges product, solutions, and capacity planning to reduce SLA churn and unexpected cost overruns.

acceptance_criteria:
A single-page negotiation cheat sheet for Sales/Solutions with recommended GPU families by workload fingerprint (exploration, short-burst evals, continuous fine-tune).
A template SLA clause set: committed throughput (tokens/sec), p50/p95 latency targets, burst credit accounting, and defined fallback model tiers with explicit degradation behavior.
Onboarding checklist with required telemetry and sample traces (warm-start times, effective batch sizes, inter-step waiting) to qualify customers into priority lanes.
Two worked examples mapping real customer telemetry to recommended reservation sizes and autoscale policies (one small fintech customer; one large marketplace).
Handover artifacts for Capacity Engineering: expected GPU affinity, expected KV cache warmup sequence, and checkpoint restore windows.
Enable Solutions to close at least 3 pilot reservations with <15% post-onboard SLA revision rate in the quarter following rollout.

success_metrics:
Pilot reservation SLA amendments reduced from 30% to <15% within 90 days
Average time from intake to production reservation reduced from 18 days to 10 days
Customer-reported cost variance vs. estimated <10% after 1 month of steady state
Support escalations for unexpected cold-starts reduced by 50% for RLHF/fine-tune customers

implementation_notes:
Introduce a compact workload fingerprint form (CSV + sample trace) ingestible by capacity recommender service (PM-166841 dependency).
Recommend GPU classes: H100 for heavy cross-GPU model-parallel RLHF; A100-80GB for medium multi-GPU fine-tune; L4 for lightweight evaluation-only cohorts. Include quantization caveats for warm-start behavior.
Define burst accounting: implement a 'burst credit' ledger that decrements when customer usage exceeds committed throughput and replenishes weekly; document auto-fallback to lower-cost variant when no burst credits remain.
Autoscale policy suggested: primary reserved pool (committed GPUs) + warm standby nodes (pre-warmed checkpoints) with a 5–10 minute spin-up SLA for additional GPUs; provide recipe for checkpoint warmers using our orchestration hooks.
Cost guidance: show three pricing profiles (conservative, balanced, aggressive) with expected monthly $/commit and estimated overage exposure.

risks:
Underestimating checkpoint IO may cause sustained tail latency increases not captured by steady-state token metrics.
Customers may over-commit to H100 class to avoid latency risk, increasing margin pressure if traffic characteristics change.
Complex negotiation clauses (burst credits + fallbacks) may slow sales cycles without clear calculator tooling.
Fallback to lower-cost model variant can cause quality regressions; needs explicit evaluation examples in the SLA.

monitoring:
Add a dedicated dashboard tile: committed throughput vs observed tokens/sec (1m/5m/1h) with burst-credit balance overlay.
Instrument warm-start metric: time from allocation to first token served per checkpoint (goal < 90s for pre-warmed standby).
Expose p50/p95/p99 latency per model-variant and per route; flag deviations >25% from SLA for automatic alerting.
Collect KV cache hit-rate and effective batch size to correlate cost and latency changes.

rollout_plan:
Week 1: Draft cheat sheet and intake form; review with Solutions (2 sessions).
Week 2: Validate two historical customer telemetry sets; produce worked examples with Capacity Eng.
Week 3: Create Sales negotiation script and one-pager; publish to internal Confluence and schedule training.
Week 4: Pilot with two inbound enterprise requests; collect feedback and iterate the playbook.
Post-pilot: Automate key calculations into capacity recommender (follow-up PM ticket).

testing_plan:
Run three synthetic burst scenarios against staging dedicated pools to validate burst-credit accounting and fallback behavior.
Simulate checkpoint restores and measure warm-start times across GPU families and network-attached storage options.
A/B test two autoscale policies (immediate ephemeral spin-up vs. warm standby) and report cost/latency trade-offs.
Coordinate with Solutions to run a dry negotiation with a friendly customer and refine script.

decisions:
Adopt a hybrid SLA model: committed throughput + burst credits rather than pure max-throughput commitments.
Default recommended GPU family mapping will be conservative (H100 for cross-GPU RLHF) with explicit cost delta disclosure.
Include an explicit 'quality-at-fallback' annex in SLA describing expected output degradation and rollback triggers.

next_steps:
Finalize the one-pager and negotiation script; circulate to Sales and Solutions by 2026-03-17.
Create two worked examples with cost math and publish in the Confluence playbook.
Open follow-up PM ticket to integrate the burst-credit model into the capacity recommender: dependency on PM-166841.
Schedule pilot onboarding sessions with the two customers for week of 2026-03-22 and instrument dashboards.

progress_updates:
2026-03-04: Kickoff meeting with Solutions and Capacity Eng. Agreed on primary deliverables and two pilot customers.
2026-03-07: Collected telemetry from pilot-cust-A (RLHF nightly bursts) and pilot-cust-B (incremental fine-tune loops).
2026-03-10: Drafted negotiation cheat-sheet and initial SLA clause language; reviewed with Legal for high-level compliance concerns.
2026-03-12: Validated warm-start numbers on staging using H100 and A100 pools; discovered checkpoint IO is the dominant variance factor.
2026-03-13: Updated playbook to include 'checkpoint warmer' orchestration snippet and added fallback model quality examples.
